title: Universal locally closed pullback locus for an invertible module
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base] of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every morphism $g:T\to S$, form the cartesian square $X_T=X\times_S T$ with projections $p:X_T\to T$ and $q:X_T\to X$. Assume that for every such $g$ the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to p_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism. For a finite locally free module $\mathcal E$ on $X$, there is an immersion $j:Z\to S$ of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] such that a morphism $g:T\to S$ factors through $Z$ if and only if there exists a finite locally free module $\mathcal N$ on $T$ with an isomorphism $q^*\mathcal E\cong p^*\mathcal N$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma diagonal-picard-flat-proper, Tag 0BDP

proof.text: Construct j:W to S representing the universal simultaneous direct-image rank and base-change condition P. Give the immersion, local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness properties to instance synthesis.

For every h:T to W, the representing equivalence gives P(f,E,h followed by j). Construct the retrocompact evaluation-isomorphism open k:Z to W. The composite k followed by j is an immersion, locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the Mathlib composition instances.

If g factors through k followed by j via l, reassociate its factorization and apply both representing equivalences. P gives finite local freeness of the actual module N=p_*q*E. The invertible counit gives q*E isomorphic to p*N by the inverse of asIso(counit). This constructs the required N without choosing data from an existence theorem.

Conversely, given a finite locally free N and q*E isomorphic to p*N, apply the pullback-evaluation implication to obtain P and an invertible counit. P gives h:T to W with h followed by j equal to g. Substitute this equality into the counit condition; the open-locus equivalence gives l:T to Z with l followed by k equal to h. Composition and associativity prove l followed by (k followed by j) equal to g.

lean.statement: theorem picard_diagonal_locally_closed {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (hO : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S), IsIso ((Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.snd f g))).unit.app (SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf))) (E : X.Modules) [E.IsFiniteLocallyFree] : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (j : Z ⟶ S), IsImmersion j ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧ QuasiSeparated j ∧ ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S), (∃ (h : T ⟶ Z), h ≫ j = g) ↔ ∃ (N : T.Modules) (_ : N.IsFiniteLocallyFree), Nonempty (((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj E) ≅ ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.snd f g)).obj N))
